open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes input
open_points.text: “module:surface turns every JSON text a request carries … into its canonical form with canonical_values.canonical_bytes” / “Inputs: One JSON value.” / “refuse … a duplicate key”
open_points.question: Does canonical_bytes receive raw JSON text capable of preserving duplicate keys, or an already parsed JSON value in which duplicate keys have been lost?
options: Receive raw JSON text at surface calls and parsed values at internal calls
Always receive raw JSON text
Always receive parsed values and detect duplicate keys before this operation
open_points.default_guess: Use separate raw-text parsing at the surface, then let canonical_bytes accept parsed values internally.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.canonical_bytes failure code
open_points.text: “a text JCS cannot represent is invalid_request” / “Errors: refused for a value JCS cannot represent” / “module:surface returns it unchanged except internal_error and stop_required”
open_points.question: When canonical_bytes rejects request data, does the MCP caller receive invalid_request or refused, and who performs that translation?
options: Surface translates this refusal to invalid_request
canonical_bytes returns invalid_request for surface input
The caller receives refused unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Surface returns invalid_request for request data and internal callers translate the same canonicalization failure into their domain outcome.

open_points.subject: canonical_values.content_identity dispatch
open_points.text: “Inputs: One content record's meaning facts … or one value.”
open_points.question: How does the operation distinguish a raw value digest from a StoredValue value_id, request_digest, idempotency key, or a model identity, each of which hashes different meaning facts and applies different list-order rules?
options: Pass an explicit identity kind with the facts
Use distinct typed input variants whose type determines the identity rule
Infer the rule from the JSON object's shape
open_points.default_guess: Use explicit typed variants; raw values produce value_digest, while model meaning facts produce that model's identity.

open_points.subject: content identity and proof ordering for tied edges or constants
open_points.text: “edges in the edge order of A05, constants by (to_node, to_port)” / “edges, by (to_node, to_port, from_node, from_port)”
open_points.question: What breaks ties between constants targeting the same port or edges with the same endpoints but different guards, so flow_version_id and the first proof failure are deterministic?
options: Use the canonical bytes of the whole constant or edge as a final tie-breaker
Preserve author-supplied order for tied items
Refuse tied keys during composition
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical bytes of the complete item as the final tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case file inputs
open_points.text: “Inputs: A contract version, input values by port, optional expected outputs, the actor.” / “A check is given a file as facts — digest, size, media type — never bytes.”
open_points.question: How are authored file-fixture bytes supplied to add_trial_case so the operation can publish them in the content-addressed area?
options: Pass file bytes together with their facts
Have surface publish the bytes first and pass StoredValue references
Pass facts plus a separate byte-source capability
open_points.default_guess: Pass the fixture bytes with their declared facts and verify them before publishing.

open_points.subject: functions.add_trial_case expected outputs
open_points.text: “optional expected outputs” / “expected_outputs: StoredValues by output port … absent when only the absence of failure is required”
open_points.question: When expected_outputs is present, must it contain every contract output port, or may it assert only a subset?
options: It must contain exactly every output port
It may contain any non-empty subset and only those outputs are compared
It may be empty but present, distinct from absent
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly every output port when expected_outputs is present.

open_points.subject: flows.compose_flow_version constants
open_points.text: “Inputs: A flow name, a purpose when new, ports, nodes, edges, guards, constants with declared classes, the actor.” / “A constant's StoredValue takes the value_schema and class the composing agent declared with it.”
open_points.question: Where does each constant's declared value_schema come from, since the operation's input lists only its declared class?
options: Each constant input includes both value_schema and disclosure_class
The schema is copied from its target port
The schema is inferred from the literal value
open_points.default_guess: Require every constant to carry its explicitly declared value_schema and disclosure_class.

open_points.subject: SpooledFile lookup identity
open_points.text: “Substitution: equal facts are the same spooled file.” / “A SpooledFile is named by its producing position alone (SpooledFileKey)” / “its digest, size and media type are not asked”
open_points.question: Is a SpooledFile identified by all M22 facts, including digest, size and media type, or solely by its producing-position key?
options: Producing-position key is the lookup identity; content facts are record attributes
All M22 facts form the identity and must be supplied
Use a separately minted SpooledFile identity
open_points.default_guess: Use the producing-position key as the unique lookup identity and return content facts from the record.

open_points.subject: runs.continue_after_approval effect
open_points.text: “Observable effect: An approved effect is sent in this request” / “a pre-send check may still fail and leave the approval unused”
open_points.question: Does approving guarantee that an HTTP request leaves the kernel, or only that the element is reached again and sent if all rebuilt pre-send checks pass?
options: Only re-reach is guaranteed; a pre-send failure sends nothing
Approval bypasses subsequent pre-send failures and guarantees a send
A pre-send failure makes the approval decision itself fail and roll back
open_points.default_guess: Only re-reach is guaranteed; pre-send failure records operation_failed and leaves the approval unused.

open_points.subject: runs.resume_run effect
open_points.text: “Observable effect: Elements waiting on an unreachable service are sent again.” / “an element whose grant was revoked meanwhile waits for approval instead”
open_points.question: Does resume guarantee a new HTTP send for every service_unreachable element, or merely re-reach each element so current authority and pre-send checks may prevent sending?
options: Re-reach every element; sending is conditional
Guarantee one new HTTP request per waiting element
Skip elements lacking current authority but leave their old wait unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Re-reach each element in order; sending occurs only if current authority and pre-send checks allow it.
